title: QC configuration
purpose: Inspect six types of laboratory configuration controlling preservation, independent preparation, holding clocks, QC frequencies/limits and result qualifiers.

sections.title: Access
paragraphs: These are staff pages. Active users with an application staff role can read them; client accounts cannot. Analysts perform result entry and batch work, reviewers decide results, and administrators maintain configuration. Administrators also have operational analyst and reviewer access, but independence rules still apply. Superuser status alone does not grant an application role.

items.label: Method
items.description: All methods by default; choices include inactive method versions. Filters preservation rules, independent preparation requirements, holding rules, QC requirements and QC limits. It does not filter result qualifiers.

items.label: Apply
items.description: Apply the selected method across five tables. An invalid method shows an error and no rows in those five tables; qualifiers remain visible.

items.label: Clear all
items.description: Restore all methods.

items.label: Columns
items.description: Each table has its own browser-saved visibility/order dialog and Reset columns. Identifier columns stay available. These tables have no sortable header links.

items.label: Rows per page
items.description: Only QC limits are paginated: 25 by default, 50 or 100. Their page links retain the method filter. Other tables show their full selected sets.

items.label: Test
items.description: Exact test definition (method/version, analyte and matrix); opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Temperature
items.description: Configured range with lower/upper/unit, No temperature requirement, or Manual temperature assessment.

items.label: Source / applicability
items.description: Method/SOP source and applicability text used in assessment evidence.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether the rule is used in current screening.

items.label: Add preservation rule
items.description: Administrators create a rule for one exact test. No configured rule does not imply acceptance; chemical/container requirements remain manual.

items.label: Test
items.description: Exact analytical test definition; opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Preparation method
items.description: Required exact preparation method/version for new observations.

items.label: Source / applicability
items.description: Laboratory source and applicability.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether new observations require an explicit prepared aliquot.

items.label: Add preparation requirement
items.description: Administrators link a test to its independent preparation method. No requirement does not establish that physical preparation is unnecessary.

items.label: Rule
items.description: Rule name; opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Method
items.description: Exact method/version.

items.label: Matrix
items.description: Water, Wastewater or Soil.

items.label: From → to
items.description: Collection/composite end or Preparation start through Preparation start or Analysis start.

items.label: Maximum
items.description: Configured maximum duration; optional warning shows the remaining-time threshold.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether the clock is applied to new evaluations.

items.label: Add holding-time rule
items.description: Administrators define an explicit clock. No active rule gives a not-evaluated holding status, not a fabricated threshold.

items.label: Method
items.description: Exact method/version; opens that type’s requirement for administrators.

items.label: QC type
items.description: Configured QC sample type.

items.label: Minimum per batch
items.description: Minimum count for the type.

items.label: One per N samples
items.description: Optional additional sample-frequency count; required total is the greater of the minimum and rounded-up samples/N.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether the frequency is enforced.

items.label: Add QC requirement
items.description: Administrators create a frequency requirement. With none configured, no QC sample frequency is enforced.

items.label: Test
items.description: Exact definition; phase Analysis or Preparation appears beneath it. Opens edit for administrators.

items.label: QC type
items.description: Type whose measure is evaluated.

items.label: Measure
items.description: Measured value, Percent recovery or Relative percent difference.

items.label: Lower
items.description: Inclusive lower acceptance bound, or a dash if none.

items.label: Upper
items.description: Inclusive upper acceptance bound, or a dash if none.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether current QC evaluation uses the limit.

items.label: Add QC limit
items.description: Administrators create bounds for the exact test, phase, QC type and measure. Missing applicable limits produce Not evaluated and hold approval.

items.label: Code
items.description: Result qualifier code; opens edit for administrators.

items.label: Description
items.description: Meaning captured into a result revision when used.

items.label: Marks holding-time exceedance
items.description: Whether this qualifier can identify a result’s exceeded holding time for submission/review checks.

items.label: Active
items.description: Whether new entries may select the code.

items.label: Add qualifier
items.description: Administrators define a code and meaning. Qualifiers are not filtered by method.

sections.title: Policy and history
paragraphs: Only administrators can save configuration. Existing edits require a reason, preserve before/after audit values and reject stale edit forms. Inactive rows remain listed. Configuration represents lab-owned policy, not regulatory defaults; synthetic seed values are not validated. Frozen result/report snapshots retain their earlier values, while current QC and preservation checks can change approval/release eligibility. Empty sections explain the consequence of absent configuration and offer Add controls to administrators.
